title: Bài sưu tầm 334 - Passage 3: Why Truly Original Science Is Hard to Spot
passageHtml:
READING PASSAGE 334

Why Truly Original Science Is Hard to Spot

Paragraph 1. Ask the public how major scientific discoveries happen, and the answer usually involves a lone genius experiencing a sudden flash of inspiration. Yet historians and sociologists who study research output paint a very different picture. In an analysis of millions of academic papers, sociologist Dashun Wang found that breakthroughs rarely follow a tidy schedule; fortunate accidents, unexpected side-results, and timing play a much larger part than funding bodies care to admit. Even more unsettling for policy makers is evidence that the most disruptive ideas often look unpromising—or downright mistaken—when they first appear.

Paragraph 2. To measure this delayed recognition, researchers track what they call 'sleeping beauties' in scientific literature: studies that sit practically unread for decades before suddenly sparking a wave of citations. A paper on bacterial immune defence published in the late 1980s attracted little notice for nearly twenty years until a separate laboratory realised those odd genetic repeats could be adapted into the CRISPR gene-editing tool. When an idea arrives before supporting instruments or neighbouring fields are ready to use it, its value remains invisible, regardless of how rigorous the initial work is.

Paragraph 3. Modern funding structures unintentionally make matters worse. When grant committees evaluate proposals, reviewers naturally favour projects whose methods and likely results resemble established consensus. Proposals that challenge core assumptions face split opinions among referees, and because committees typically demand near-unanimous approval before committing large budgets, bold ventures lose out to safe, incremental studies. As physicist Freeman Dyson warned, judging science strictly by short-term predictability rewards tidy bookkeeping at the expense of genuine exploration.

Paragraph 4. At the same time, the structure of scientific labour itself is changing. A landmark study of twenty million papers and patents revealed that whereas solo authors once produced many major advances, contemporary breakthroughs overwhelmingly emerge from multi-person groups pooling specialised skills. Yet team size introduces a subtle trade-off. Large consortia excel at developing and testing existing theories thoroughly, whereas smaller, tight-knit groups remain statistically more likely to disrupt a field with an unconventional leap. University departments frequently measure output by counting publications in elite journals, yet those metrics rarely distinguish between steady refinement and genuine conceptual novelty. To keep discovery alive, institutions may need to reserve a portion of their budgets for high-uncertainty projects judged by curiosity rather than immediate certainty.

q27.text: What does Dashun Wang's research suggest about scientific breakthroughs?
options: A. Individual brilliance accounts for almost every major discovery.
B. Chance events influence outcomes more than grant agencies acknowledge.
C. Older papers are cited more accurately than modern studies.
D. Public surveys accurately capture how researchers work.

steps: Đoạn 1: Tai nạn may mắn và thời điểm đóng vai trò lớn hơn nhiều so với mức các tổ chức tài trợ muốn thừa nhận (fortunate accidents... play a much larger part than funding bodies care to admit).
Kết luận: Chọn B.

q28.text: Why does the writer mention a 1980s paper on bacteria in the second paragraph?
options: A. To show that early gene-editing tools contained serious flaws.
B. To illustrate how rival laboratories often duplicate each other's work.
C. To prove that poorly written studies are rightly ignored by peers.
D. To give an example of research whose importance became clear much later.

steps: Đoạn 2: Minh họa cho hiện tượng 'sleeping beauties': bài báo nằm im gần 20 năm mới được nhận ra giá trị khi ghép vào công cụ CRISPR.
Kết luận: Chọn D.

q29.text: According to paragraph 3, why are daring research proposals frequently rejected?
options: A. Scoring systems penalise projects when reviewers disagree.
B. Committee members lack technical knowledge in new fields.
C. Innovative projects usually exceed university laboratory space.
D. Reviewers prefer applicants with longer publication records.

steps: Đoạn 3: Đề xuất táo bạo gây ý kiến trái chiều giữa các giám khảo, trong khi hội đồng lại đòi hỏi sự đồng thuận gần như tuyệt đối nên bị loại (face split opinions... committees typically demand near-unanimous approval).
Kết luận: Chọn A.
Đoạn 1: fortunate accidents ↔ luck (I).
Đoạn 2: attracted little notice ↔ little immediate attention (E).
Đoạn 3: favour projects whose methods... resemble established consensus ↔ show a bias (F) against unconventional plans.
Đoạn 3: committing large budgets... bold ventures lose out to safe... studies ↔ take a financial risk (A).
Đoạn 4: emerge from multi-person groups pooling specialised skills ↔ large-scale teamwork (C).
Đoạn 2: sit practically unread for decades... value remains invisible ↔ unavoidable delay (B).

q36.text: Genuinely groundbreaking ideas are usually recognised immediately by fellow experts.

steps: Đoạn 1: Những ý tưởng đột phá nhất lúc mới xuất hiện thường trông kém hứa hẹn hoặc thậm chí bị coi là sai lầm (often look unpromising—or downright mistaken—when they first appear).
Kết luận: Chọn NO.

q37.text: Current funding procedures tend to support research that stays close to accepted theories.

steps: Đoạn 3: Hội đồng thiên vị các dự án giống với đồng thuận sẵn có và an toàn (favour projects whose methods and likely results resemble established consensus).
Kết luận: Chọn YES.

q38.text: Smaller research teams publish more papers in elite journals than large consortia.

steps: Đoạn 4: Bài có nói về nhóm nhỏ dễ tạo đột phá (smaller, tight-knit groups... disrupt a field) và có nhắc đến việc đếm bài trên tạp chí danh tiếng (counting publications in elite journals), nhưng không nói nhóm nhỏ đăng nhiều bài trên đó hơn nhóm lớn.
Kết luận: Chọn NOT GIVEN.

q39.text: Large collaborative groups are better suited to expanding known ideas than overturning them.

steps: Đoạn 4: "Large consortia excel at developing and testing existing theories thoroughly, whereas smaller... groups remain statistically more likely to disrupt a field..."
Kết luận: Chọn YES.

q40.text: Which title best reflects the main message of Reading Passage 334?
options: A. How lone scientists are replacing modern university teams
B. Why biological discoveries take longer than physics breakthroughs
C. Why current systems struggle to recognise unconventional research
D. The rising cost of laboratory equipment in contemporary science

steps: Chủ đề xuyên suốt bài: Các cơ chế đánh giá và tài trợ hiện tại khó nhận diện được nghiên cứu đột phá phi truyền thống.
Kết luận: Chọn C.
